source.text: Ἀπεκρίνατο οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ δύναται ὁ υἱὸς ποιεῖν ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ οὐδὲν ἐὰν μή τι βλέπῃ τὸν πατέρα ποιοῦντα· ἃ γὰρ ἂν ἐκεῖνος ποιῇ, ταῦτα καὶ ὁ υἱὸς ὁμοίως ποιεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: Answered therefore the Jesus and was saying to them, "Truly truly I say to you, not is able the Son to do from himself nothing if not anything he may see the Father doing; what for ever that [one] may do, these things also the Son likewise does.

en.L: So Jesus answered and said to them, "Truly, truly I say to you, the Son is not able to do anything from {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, except what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sees the Father doing; for whatever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does, these things the Son also does likewise.
en.B: So Jesus gave them this answer: "Truly, truly, I tell you, the Son cannot do anything on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does only what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sees the Father doing. For what the Father does, the Son does as well, and in the same way.
en.R: Jesus answered them, "I tell you the truth: the Son cannot do anything just on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own. He does only what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sees the Father doing. Whatever the Father does, the Son does the same.

decisions.choice: Jesus answers the charge of 5:18
decisions.reason: The authorities wanted to kill Jesus because he called God his own Father, "making himself equal with God" (5:18). He does not take the claim back. He explains it: the Son's equality with the Father is not a rival claim to power but a complete unity of action, in which the Son does whatever the Father does (this verse) and receives the honor the Father receives (5:23).

decisions.choice: from himself: on his own, apart from the Father
alternatives: by his own power, as if the Son lacked ability
decisions.reason: The phrase ἀφ ἑαυτοῦ means acting on one's own initiative or authority, as in 7:17-18, 11:51, 14:10 and 16:13. The "cannot" describes the Son's relationship to the Father, not a lack of power: the Son never acts as a separate agent, because he and the Father act together (10:30; 14:10). Jesus says the same of himself in 5:30.

decisions.choice: whatever the Father does, the Son does the same works, in the same way
alternatives: the Son imitates the Father, doing similar things
decisions.reason: The pronoun ἐκεῖνος ("that one") refers to the Father. The sentence does not say the Son does similar things, but "these things", the very works the Father does, and "likewise". The next verses name two of them, giving life to the dead and judging (5:21-22), which in Scripture belong to God alone.

decisions.choice: Truly, truly I say to you (L); Truly, truly, I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering for John (see 1:51), recorded once in this passage; it covers 5:24 and 5:25 as well.

decisions.choice: on his own
decisions.reason: Plain English for the idiom (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps "from himself", the Greek form. 5:30 uses the same wording.

decisions.choice: the Father
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Father for the pronoun "that one", so the reader does not lose track of who is meant (meaning decision m3). Literal has "he".

decisions.choice: said (L); gave them this answer (B)
decisions.reason: "Answered and was saying" is a common way of introducing a reply; the second verb adds no separate action. Literal keeps both verbs and gives the second in the simple past.

source.text: ὁ γὰρ πατὴρ φιλεῖ τὸν υἱὸν καὶ πάντα δείκνυσιν αὐτῷ ἃ αὐτὸς ποιεῖ, καὶ μείζονα τούτων δείξει αὐτῷ ἔργα, ἵνα ὑμεῖς θαυμάζητε.

records.literal_gloss: The for Father loves the Son and all things shows to him which he himself does, and greater than these he will show him works, so that you may marvel.

en.L: For the Father loves the Son and shows {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all things that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} does, and greater works than these {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will show {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that you may marvel.
en.B: For the Father loves the Son and shows {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} is doing. And there are greater works than these that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will show {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that you will be astonished.
en.R: The Father loves the Son and shows {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will show {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} even greater works than these. Then you will be amazed.

decisions.choice: loves: the Father's love for the Son
alternatives: affection or friendship, a lesser love than the other verb
decisions.reason: φιλεῖ is one of John's two verbs for love. John uses both of the Father's love for the Son: 3:35 has the other verb, this verse has this one. Here, as there, the meaning is the same, so there is no difference in kind between the two (see the note at 21:15-17). The love is the reason the Father hides nothing from the Son.

decisions.choice: greater works: giving life to the dead and judging (5:21-29)
alternatives: only further and more striking signs, such as the raising of Lazarus
decisions.reason: "These" are works like the healing at the pool that started the dispute (5:1-9). The next sentences, which begin "for", say what is greater: raising the dead and giving them life, and carrying out judgment. The raising of Lazarus (11:43-44) is a sign of this greater work.

decisions.choice: so that you may marvel: astonishment, which is not yet belief
decisions.reason: The pronoun ὑμεῖς is stated, so it is emphatic: you, the very people who oppose him. Amazement at what Jesus does may lead to believing, or it may stop short of it; in 5:28 he tells them not to marvel, and in 7:21 the crowd marvels at one work and is still divided. Marveling is not the goal; believing is (5:24).

decisions.choice: astonished (B); amazed (R)
decisions.reason: Everyday words for marveling. Literal keeps "marvel". 5:28 uses the same words for the same verb.

decisions.choice: And there are greater works than these that he will show him
alternatives: And he will show him greater works than these
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the stress the Greek puts on "greater" by putting the works first.

source.text: ὥσπερ γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ἐγείρει τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ ζῳοποιεῖ, οὕτως καὶ ὁ υἱὸς οὓς θέλει ζῳοποιεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: Just as for the Father raises the dead and gives life, so also the Son whom he wills gives life.

en.L: For just as the Father raises the dead and gives [them] life, so also the Son gives life to whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wills.
en.B: For the Father raises the dead and brings them to life, and in the same way the Son brings to life whomever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses.
en.R: The Father raises people from the dead and gives them life. In the same way, the Son gives life to anyone {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants to.

decisions.choice: raising the dead and giving life is God's own work, and the Son does it
decisions.reason: In Scripture it is God who kills and makes alive, who brings down to the grave and raises up (Deuteronomy 32:39; 1 Samuel 2:6); the king of Israel asks, "Am I God, to kill and to make alive?" (2 Kings 5:7). By saying the Son does the same, Jesus answers the charge that he makes himself equal with God (5:18).

decisions.choice: gives life: both raising to bodily life and giving eternal life now
alternatives: only the resurrection at the last day
decisions.reason: ζῳοποιεῖ means to make alive. The following verses use both senses: those who hear his word already have eternal life and have passed from death to life (5:24-25), and at the last day those in the tombs will come out (5:28-29).

decisions.choice: whom he wills: the Son gives life freely, and his will is one with the Father's
alternatives: the Son chooses independently of the Father
decisions.reason: The Son is not a tool that the Father uses; he gives life by his own choice. But his will is never separate from the Father's: he seeks only the will of the one who sent him (5:30), and the Father's will is that everyone who looks to the Son and believes in him should have eternal life (6:40). The sentence does not say how the choice is made.

decisions.choice: [them] (L); them (B, R)
decisions.reason: English needs an object for "gives life" after "raises the dead".

decisions.choice: chooses (B); wants to (R)
decisions.reason: "Wills" is formal; these words say the same thing in everyday English.

source.text: οὐδὲ γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ κρίνει οὐδένα, ἀλλὰ τὴν κρίσιν πᾶσαν δέδωκεν τῷ υἱῷ, ἵνα πάντες τιμῶσι τὸν υἱὸν καθὼς τιμῶσι τὸν πατέρα.

records.literal_gloss: Not even for the Father judges no one, but the judgment all he has given to the Son, \v 23 so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father.

en.L: For neither does the Father judge anyone, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given all judgment to the Son, \v 23 so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father.
en.B: Nor does the Father judge anyone; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given the whole work of judging to the Son, \v 23 so that everyone will honor the Son just as they honor the Father.
en.R: The Father does not judge anyone. He has put all judging into the Son's hands, \v 23 so that everyone will honor the Son just as they honor the Father.

decisions.choice: the Father judges no one: he judges through the Son, not apart from him
alternatives: the Father has no part in judgment at all
decisions.reason: "For neither" ties this to 5:21: as the Son gives life, so also judging is in his hands. Scripture calls God the judge of all the earth (Genesis 18:25), and Jesus later says that the Father "seeks and judges" (8:50). So the point is not that the Father has nothing to do with judgment, but that he carries it out through the Son.

decisions.choice: all judgment: the whole work of judging, deciding and passing sentence
decisions.reason: κρίσιν is the act and authority of judging, here without limit ("all"). The perfect δέδωκεν speaks of a gift already made and still in force. 5:27 says the same gift is "authority to carry out judgment".

decisions.choice: the Son receives the honor given to God
decisions.reason: "Just as" means the same honor, not a lesser one. In Isaiah 42:8 the LORD says he will not give his glory to another; yet the Father wills that the Son be honored as he is. This is the heart of Jesus's answer to 5:18.

decisions.choice: given the whole work of judging (B); put all judging into the Son's hands (R)
decisions.reason: Makes clear that "all judgment" is the task and right of judging, not a single verdict (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: everyone
decisions.reason: The Greek word means all people; "everyone" is already inclusive and needs no setting.

source.text: ὁ μὴ τιμῶν τὸν υἱὸν οὐ τιμᾷ τὸν πατέρα τὸν πέμψαντα αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] not honoring the Son not honors the Father the [one] having sent him.

en.L: The one who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Whoever refuses honor to the Son refuses it to the Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Anyone who does not honor the Son is not honoring the Father either, because the Father is the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: how an envoy is treated is how the sender is treated
decisions.reason: In the ancient world a messenger stood for the one who sent him. When the Ammonite king shamed David's envoys, David took it as done to himself (2 Samuel 10:1-5). Jesus says the same of his own messengers (13:20; Matthew 10:40). The Son is the Father's envoy, so dishonoring him dishonors the Father.

decisions.choice: the Father who sent him: the Son comes on the Father's mission
decisions.reason: "The one who sent me" is one of Jesus's commonest names for the Father in John (5:24, 30, 37; 6:38-39). It ties the Son's words and works to the Father's purpose.

decisions.choice: refuses honor ... refuses it
alternatives: does not honor ... does not honor (Literal)
decisions.reason: Keeps the repeated verb but makes the sentence run in Balanced.

decisions.choice: because the Father is the one who sent him
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the link that "who sent him" implies (meaning decision m1).

source.text: Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ὁ τὸν λόγον μου ἀκούων καὶ πιστεύων τῷ πέμψαντί με ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον, καὶ εἰς κρίσιν οὐκ ἔρχεται ἀλλὰ μεταβέβηκεν ἐκ τοῦ θανάτου εἰς τὴν ζωήν.

records.literal_gloss: Truly truly I say to you that the [one] the word of me hearing and believing the [one] having sent me has life eternal, and into judgment not comes but has passed out of the death into the life.

en.L: Truly, truly I say to you, the one who hears {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word and believes the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has eternal life, and does not come into judgment, but has passed out of death into life.
en.B: Truly, truly, I tell you, anyone who hears {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word and believes the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has eternal life. Such a person does not come under condemnation, but has already moved out of death into life.
en.R: I tell you the truth: anyone who hears what I say and believes the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} already has eternal life. That person will not be judged guilty. {{gender:They have|He has}} left death behind and come into life.

decisions.choice: one person who both hears the Son's word and believes the Father
decisions.reason: One article governs both verbs: hearing and believing describe the same person. To believe "the one who sent me" is to trust the Father's testimony, which is heard in the Son's word (5:37-38; 12:44). Hearing here is hearing that takes the word in, as in 5:25 and 10:27.

decisions.choice: has eternal life: possessed now
alternatives: will have eternal life at the last day
decisions.reason: The verb is present: the one who believes has eternal life already, not only after death (3:36; 6:47). Eternal life is the life of the age to come, knowing the Father and the one he sent (17:3).

decisions.choice: judgment: condemnation, the verdict that goes against someone
alternatives: any judgment at all, so that believers are never examined
decisions.reason: Set against eternal life and passing from death to life, κρίσιν here is a judgment that condemns, as in 3:18-19 and "the resurrection of judgment" in 5:29. The sentence does not deny that all people stand before the Son as judge (5:22, 27); it says that for the one who believes, the outcome is not condemnation.

decisions.choice: has passed from death to life: a move already made, whose result stands
alternatives: will pass from death to life at the resurrection
decisions.reason: μεταβέβηκεν is perfect: the crossing has happened and its result remains. Death here is the state of being cut off from God's life, in which a person lives before believing; 1 John 3:14 uses the same words of believers. Bodily death still lies ahead (11:25), but it cannot undo this life.

decisions.choice: come under condemnation (B); be judged guilty (R)
decisions.reason: Gives the sense of judgment here (meaning decision m3), as in 3:17-18. Literal keeps "judgment" so the word family of 5:22-30 stays visible.

decisions.choice: already
decisions.reason: Brings out the present "has" and the perfect "has passed" (meaning decisions m2 and m4).

decisions.choice: {{gender:They have|He has}}
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and needs a pronoun for anyone who believes; inclusive default. Literal and Balanced need none.

decisions.choice: what I say
decisions.reason: Plain words for "my word": the whole of Jesus's message.

source.text: Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἔρχεται ὥρα καὶ νῦν ἐστιν ὅτε οἱ νεκροὶ ἀκούσουσιν τῆς φωνῆς τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ οἱ ἀκούσαντες ζήσουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Truly truly I say to you that is coming an hour and now is when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of the God and the [ones] having heard will live.

en.L: Truly, truly I say to you, an hour is coming, and now is, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
en.B: Truly, truly, I tell you, an hour is coming, and in fact it has already begun, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear it will live.
en.R: I tell you the truth: a time is coming, and it has already started, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God. Those who listen to it will live.

decisions.choice: an hour is coming and now is: the time God has set for giving life, already begun in Jesus
decisions.reason: As at 4:23, the hour is still ahead and yet has already begun with Jesus present. This is not Jesus's own appointed hour, the hour of his death and glory (2:4; 12:23), but the time God has fixed for the dead to hear and live. 5:28 speaks of the same hour without "and now is".

decisions.choice: the dead: those who are spiritually dead, who hear the Son now and receive life
alternatives: the physically dead, raised during Jesus's ministry
the dead at the last day
decisions.reason: "And now is" puts this in the present, and 5:24 has just spoken of passing from death to life by hearing the Son's word. So the dead here are people without God's life, who come alive when they hear him (compare Ephesians 2:1, 5). Jesus's raising of the physically dead, such as Lazarus (11:43-44), is a sign of this. In 5:28-29 the bodily dead are meant.

decisions.choice: will hear ... those who hear: the voice reaches them; those who heed it live
decisions.reason: Not everyone who hears lives: the second "hear" means hearing that takes the voice in and responds, as the sheep hear the shepherd's voice (10:3, 27). In 5:28-29, by contrast, all in the tombs hear and come out, to life or to judgment.

decisions.choice: a time
decisions.reason: As at 4:21: "hour" sounds like sixty minutes. Literal and Balanced keep "hour" so John's thread of the hour stays visible.

decisions.choice: in fact it has already begun (B); it has already started (R)
decisions.reason: As at 4:23: plain words for the hour's present arrival (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Those who listen to it
decisions.reason: "Listen" brings out hearing that responds (meaning decision m3).

source.text: ὥσπερ γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ἔχει ζωὴν ἐν ἑαυτῷ, οὕτως καὶ τῷ υἱῷ ἔδωκεν ζωὴν ἔχειν ἐν ἑαυτῷ·

records.literal_gloss: Just as for the Father has life in himself, so also to the Son he gave life to have in himself;

en.L: For just as the Father has life in {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, so also {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave to the Son to have life in {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.
en.B: For just as the Father has life in {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given the Son life in {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} as well.
en.R: The Father has life in {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life does not come from anyone else. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given the Son that same life, so that the Son has it in {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} too.

decisions.choice: life in himself: life that is God's own, received from no one
decisions.reason: Everything that lives has received its life; God is the fountain of life (Psalm 36:9) and the living God (Jeremiah 10:10). "Just as ... so also" says the Son has the same life, not a lesser copy: "in him was life" (1:4). That is why the Son can give life to whom he wills (5:21).

decisions.choice: gave: the text does not say when, and leaves open whether this belongs to the Son's eternal relation to the Father or to his mission
alternatives: given to the Son only when he was sent into the world
describes only the Son's eternal relation to the Father
decisions.reason: The past tense ἔδωκεν states the gift without dating it. 1:4 says life was in the Word from the beginning, and 6:57 says the Son lives "because of the Father". The sentence teaches that the Son's life is both truly his own and received from the Father; it does not settle more than that.

decisions.choice: has given the Son life in himself
alternatives: has granted the Son also to have life in himself
decisions.reason: "Gave to the Son to have life in himself" is stiff in English; Balanced folds "to have" into "given ... life", which says the same.

decisions.choice: his life does not come from anyone else ... that same life
alternatives: has life in himself, and has given the Son to have life in himself
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "life in himself" means and that the Son's life is the same (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: has given
decisions.reason: The English perfect fits a gift whose effect continues; Literal keeps the simple past.

source.text: καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ κρίσιν ποιεῖν, ὅτι υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου ἐστίν.

records.literal_gloss: And authority he gave him judgment to do, because son of man he is.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} authority to carry out judgment, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is [the] Son of Man.
en.B: He has also given {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} authority to pass judgment, since {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the Son of Man.
en.R: The Father has also given the Son the right to judge, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the Son of Man.

decisions.choice: Son of Man: the title, the figure of Daniel 7:13-14
alternatives: because he is a human being (son of man without the title)
decisions.reason: Only here in the Gospels is the phrase without articles: literally "because he is son of man". In Hebrew "son of man" can mean simply a human being (Psalm 8:4; Ezekiel 2:1), so this could mean that the one who judges people is himself human. But the sentence is about authority given to judge, which is what Daniel 7:13-14 describes: one like a son of man is given authority, glory and an everlasting kingdom. The Greek of Daniel 7:13 also lacks the articles (as do Revelation 1:13 and 14:14). Every level keeps the title; the footnote gives "because he is a human being".

decisions.choice: Daniel 7:13-14: authority given to the one like a son of man
decisions.reason: In Daniel's vision the Ancient of Days sits in judgment (Daniel 7:9-10), and one like a son of man comes with the clouds of heaven and is given authority to rule over all peoples. Here the Father gives the Son authority to judge. The words for "authority" and "gave" match that scene.

decisions.choice: to do judgment: to carry out judgment, to act as judge
decisions.reason: κρίσιν ποιεῖν is an idiom for judging; the authority given is the authority of a judge (compare 5:22).

decisions.choice: [the] Son of Man
decisions.reason: The Greek has no articles (meaning decision m1); Literal shows that with brackets. Balanced and Readable write "the Son of Man", the book-wide title, capitalised.

decisions.choice: The Father ... the Son
decisions.reason: Readable names who gives and who receives, since the pronouns follow a long sentence.

decisions.choice: authority to pass judgment (B); the right to judge (R)
decisions.reason: Everyday wording for the idiom (meaning decision m3).

source.text: μὴ θαυμάζετε τοῦτο, ὅτι ἔρχεται ὥρα ἐν ᾗ πάντες οἱ ἐν τοῖς μνημείοις ἀκούσουσιν τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκπορεύσονται οἱ τὰ ἀγαθὰ ποιήσαντες εἰς ἀνάστασιν ζωῆς, οἱ δὲ τὰ φαῦλα πράξαντες εἰς ἀνάστασιν κρίσεως.

records.literal_gloss: Not marvel at this, because is coming an hour in which all those in the tombs will hear the voice of him \v 29 and will come out, those the good things having done to resurrection of life, those but the evil things having practiced to resurrection of judgment.

en.L: Do not marvel at this, for an hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs will hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice \v 29 and will come out, those who have done good things to a resurrection of life, but those who have practiced evil things to a resurrection of judgment.
en.B: Do not be astonished at this. An hour is coming when everyone in the tombs will hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice \v 29 and come out. Those who have done good will come out to a resurrection that brings life; those who have done evil, to a resurrection that brings condemnation.
en.R: Do not be amazed at this. A time is coming when all the dead in their graves will hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice \v 29 and come out. Those who have done good will rise from the dead and live. Those who have done evil will rise from the dead and be judged guilty.

decisions.choice: do not marvel at this: at what was just said, because of what is still to come
alternatives: do not marvel at this: that an hour is coming
decisions.reason: "This" points back to 5:25-27: that the Son gives life now and has authority to judge. The next clause gives the reason not to be amazed at it: something greater is coming. ὅτι can also introduce what "this" is ("do not marvel that an hour is coming"); the sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: an hour is coming: the bodily resurrection at the last day
decisions.reason: Unlike 5:25 there is no "and now is". Those "in the tombs" are the bodily dead, and all of them hear and come out, not only those who heed. Elsewhere Jesus speaks of raising believers "on the last day" (6:39-40, 44, 54; compare 11:24). As in 5:25, the hour is the time God has set, not Jesus's own hour.

decisions.choice: Daniel 12:2: the dead rise, some to everlasting life and some to shame
decisions.reason: Daniel 12:2 says that many who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, some to everlasting life and some to disgrace without end. Jesus takes up the same picture of two outcomes, and makes his own voice the one that wakes the dead.

decisions.choice: those who did good, those who practiced evil: deeds show how a person has responded to the Son
alternatives: life is earned by good deeds apart from believing
decisions.reason: This does not contradict 5:24, where life comes by hearing and believing. In 3:19-21 the same contrast appears: whoever practices φαῦλα hates the light, while whoever does the truth comes to the light. The work God asks is to believe in the one he sent (6:29). What people have done reveals whether they came to the light; it is not a separate way of earning life.

decisions.choice: judgment: condemnation
decisions.reason: Set against "resurrection of life", κρίσεως is the judgment that condemns, as in 5:24.

decisions.choice: A time
decisions.reason: As in 5:25. Literal and Balanced keep "hour".

decisions.choice: a resurrection that brings condemnation (B); rise from the dead and be judged guilty (R)
decisions.reason: Gives the sense of judgment here (meaning decision m5), as in 5:24.

decisions.choice: be astonished (B); be amazed (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:20, which uses the same verb.

decisions.choice: all the dead in their graves
alternatives: all who are in the tombs
decisions.reason: Readable says who is in the tombs and uses the everyday word.

decisions.choice: done evil
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "practiced" to show that the Greek uses a different verb for the evil than for the good, as in 3:20-21; the difference is one of style, and Balanced and Readable use "done" for both.

source.text: Οὐ δύναμαι ἐγὼ ποιεῖν ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐδέν· καθὼς ἀκούω κρίνω, καὶ ἡ κρίσις ἡ ἐμὴ δικαία ἐστίν, ὅτι οὐ ζητῶ τὸ θέλημα τὸ ἐμὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με.

records.literal_gloss: Not am able I to do from myself nothing; just as I hear I judge, and the judgment the mine just is, because not I seek the will the mine but the will of the [one] having sent me.

en.L: I am not able to do anything from {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}. As I hear, I judge; and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgment is just, because I do not seek {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own will, but the will of the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: I cannot do anything on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own. I judge according to what I hear, and the judgment I give is just, because I am not seeking to do {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own will, but the will of the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: I cannot do anything just on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own. I judge the way the Father tells {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to, so {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judging is right. I do not try to do what I want. I try to do what the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} wants.

decisions.choice: the Son of 5:19-29 is Jesus himself
decisions.reason: Jesus has spoken of "the Son" in the third person since 5:19; now he says "I", with the pronoun ἐγὼ stated for emphasis. The sentence repeats 5:19 ("from himself", "from myself") and closes the section.

decisions.choice: as I hear: as the Father tells him
alternatives: as he hears the evidence, like a human judge
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks and judges what he has heard from the Father (8:26, 28, 40; 12:49-50), just as he does what he sees the Father doing (5:19).

decisions.choice: his judgment is just because he seeks the will of the one who sent him
decisions.reason: A judge is fair when he has no interest of his own to serve. Jesus's food is to do the will of the one who sent him (4:34), and he came down from heaven for that purpose (6:38). So his judgment is God's own judgment.

decisions.choice: on my own
decisions.reason: As in 5:19. Literal keeps "from myself".

decisions.choice: the way the Father tells me to
decisions.reason: Readable says whom Jesus hears (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: what I want ... what the one who sent me wants
alternatives: my own will ... the will of the one who sent me
decisions.reason: Plain words for "will".

decisions.choice: right
decisions.reason: "Just" can mean "only" to young readers; "right" keeps the sense.
